examples.question_text:
Classify each number as rational or irrational, and state whether it is real.

a. $\frac{11}{4}$
b. $0.625$
c. $35\%$
d. $\sqrt{121}$
e. $\sqrt{14}$
examples.solution_text:
a. $\frac{11}{4}$ is a fraction of integers, so it is rational and real.

b. $0.625=\frac{625}{1000}=\frac{5}{8}$, so it is rational and real.

c. $35\%=\frac{35}{100}=\frac{7}{20}$, so it is rational and real.

d. $\sqrt{121}=11=\frac{11}{1}$, so it is rational and real.

e. $14$ is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{14}$ is irrational and real.

Every rational number and every irrational number is real.

examples.question_text: Write $0.\overline{36}$ as a fraction using the recurring-decimal pattern. Explain why it is rational and real.
examples.solution_text:
A two-digit repeating block uses a denominator of $99$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.\overline{36}\\&=\frac{36}{99}\\&=\frac{4}{11}\end{aligned}$

It is a fraction of integers with a non-zero denominator, so it is rational. Every rational number is real.

examples.question_text: Explain why every integer is rational. Use $-8$ as an example.
examples.solution_text:
$-8=\frac{-8}{1}$.

Every integer can be written as a fraction with denominator $1$, so every integer is rational.

examples.question_text:
Using a calculator, classify each number as rational or irrational. Explain your answers.

a. $-\frac{28.8}{8}$
b. $\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$
examples.solution_text:
a.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-\frac{28.8}{8}\\&=-3.6\\&=\frac{-18}{5}\end{aligned}$

It is a fraction of integers, so it is rational.

b.

$\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}=0.9682458\ldots$.

$15$ is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{15}$ is irrational. If $\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$ were rational, multiplying it by $4$ would make $\sqrt{15}$ rational. Therefore $\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$ is irrational.

examples.question_text:
Using a calculator, approximate each number to $2$ decimal places.

a. $\sqrt{22}$
b. $\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}$
examples.solution_text:
a. $\sqrt{22}=4.6904157\ldots$.

The third decimal digit is $0$, so $\sqrt{22}\approx4.69$.

b. $\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}=0.2773500\ldots$.

The third decimal digit is $7$, so round up: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}\approx0.28$.

examples.question_text: A student says, “$\sqrt{100}$ is irrational because it contains a square-root sign.” Explain the mistake.
examples.solution_text:
$\sqrt{100}=10=\frac{10}{1}$, so it is rational.

A square-root sign does not make a number irrational; the square root of a perfect square is rational.
